message.reasoning:
We need to analyze method crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) in NumericIndicator. It returns new CrossedUpIndicatorRule(this, other). Need to identify all possible exception scenarios.

Potential exceptions:
- other null -> NullPointerException (already covered)
- other contains NaN? The existing test includes IllegalArgumentException for NaN indicator. Need verify if CrossedUpIndicatorRule throws IllegalArgumentException when any indicator returns null or NaN. Could also be IllegalArgumentException for mismatched series length? Possibly if other has different BarSeries? The rule may require same BarSeries; if not, maybe IllegalArgumentException. So we need test case where other indicator's BarSeries differs from this's series.

- other indicator's getBarSeries() returns null? Might cause NPE inside rule.

- this delegate null? NumericIndicator's delegate is final, but could be null if constructed incorrectly? The class likely has static of method that checks null. Could test NumericIndicator.of(null) leading to NPE when calling crossedOver.

But method is instance method; if this.delegate null, rule constructor may still accept but later evaluation may NPE.

We need to add test cases for uncovered exception scenarios.

Existing cases cover null other, NaN other, same instance, same delegate but distinct instance, other indicator decreasing, multiple crossings, lagging series.

Missing: other indicator with different BarSeries causing IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException.

Also other indicator that throws exception on getValue (custom indicator that throws). That would propagate when rule is evaluated, but not at construction. The test expects exception when evaluating rule.isSatisfied.

Thus we can design test case: other indicator that throws RuntimeException when getValue called; calling crossedOver returns rule; invoking rule.isSatisfied(index) should throw that exception.

Also test for this NumericIndicator being null? Not applicable.

Also test for other indicator returning null (Num) maybe IllegalArgumentException.

Add group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator with different BarSeries.

Group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator throwing exception on getValue.

Group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator returns null value (should cause IllegalArgumentException).

Need to ensure no duplication with existing.

Now produce JSON array with groups and cases.

Each case input: parameter other with description of indicator type.

Expected: exception type.

Description accordingly.

Let's craft.

Group names: "crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator with mismatched BarSeries"

Case: other = ConstantIndicator(5) built on a different BarSeries than this NumericIndicator (which is built on a series). Expect IllegalArgumentException (or IllegalStateException). Need to decide. In TA4J, CrossedUpIndicatorRule checks that both indicators have same BarSeries; if not, it throws IllegalArgumentException. We'll assume IllegalArgumentException.

Group: "crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator throws on getValue"

Case: other = ThrowingIndicator (custom) that throws RuntimeException("test") when getValue called. Expect RuntimeException when rule.isSatisfied(index) called.

Group: "crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator returns null Num"

Case: other = NullValueIndicator (custom) returns null for getValue. Expect IllegalArgumentException when rule.isSatisfied.

Also test for this NumericIndicator constructed via of(null) leading to NPE on crossedOver. But method call on instance; if delegate null, rule may still be constructed but later NPE. Could add group: "crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - this NumericIndicator with null delegate". Input: this = NumericIndicator.of(null) (if allowed). But of likely throws IllegalArgumentException if delegate null. So not needed.

Thus produce JSON.
